android.desc:
*important: please note that this is an app for wear os (smartwatches) and not for phones! you will not be able to open this app on a phone if you purchase it without a watch*

Sometimes mapping apps overcomplicate a journey - if the only unknown variable is your train, why add layers of abstraction?

Train Tick (trainTick) is an app for wear os with the singular goal of providing up-to-date train information within the UK¹. You can find information on every upcoming train that follows a route, derived from the same data source that feeds station departure boards (so the data is always as accurate as possible).

From there, you can jump into the journey of a particular train to see where it's held up, formation data, and more!

The information is also provided as a tile, for even easier glanceability, and a quick-launch complication is available.

This app does not require connection to a phone (or for the companion app to be installed), only an internet connection! As such, it should work without issue paired with iOS as well as Android phones.

¹ Unfortunately, this app does not yet support Translink (NI) services, due to limitations of our data providers.

quotes.text:
About a year ago I made a little wear os app to track the upcoming departures at the station near me - it was suprisingly useful (especially at big stations - sometimes you can make incredibly quick connections!), so I decided to genericise it to the point it'd work for other people (in the uk) as well! So far people seem to really appreciate it [0], which I'm glad about

Alternatively, for something slightly less polished, I made an app that connects to the spotify API, fetches synced lyrics for the track currently playing, and displays them on an electromechanical (flip-dot) bus sign from the 80s that's sat in my kitchen!

[0] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=uk.nthn.android.traintimes (paid, but feel free to reach out if you want a free copy)
